chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the taslim (salutation of peace) in the two rak'ahs of al-Witr, so he said: 'If you wish, you give taslim, and if you wish, you do not give taslim.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: A title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: Taslim: The act of saying 'Assalamu Alaikum' to conclude prayer.
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْوَتْرِ: The two rak'ahs of Witr prayer.

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to say taslim at the end of the Witr prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic flexibility (ikhtiyar) in the Witr prayer, reflecting the Shia view that Witr is a confirmed Sunnah rather than a strict obligation. The Imam’s response underscores the principle of ease in worship, allowing the believer to conclude with a single salutation or two, thereby accommodating different scholarly opinions on the prayer's finalization.
